The point-fusion strategy enriches raw LiDAR points with corresponding image features prior to voxelization, while voxel-fusion combines deep features from the two modalities at a later stage in the network. Through extensive experiments on the KITTI dataset, we demonstrate that both fusion approaches significantly improve detection accuracy compared to LiDAR-only methods, particularly for challenging small objects and distant targets. MVX-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance while maintaining computational efficiency, with minimal additional latency compared to single-modality approaches. Our ablation studies reveal that the complementary information from RGB images helps overcome the sparsity limitations of point clouds, especially in scenarios with occlusion or at long ranges. This work provides valuable insights into effective multimodal fusion strategies for autonomous driving perception systems.

Small in-distribution changes in 3D perspective and lighting fool both CNNs and Transformers

Deep neural networks have demonstrated remarkable performance on computer vision tasks, yet their robustness to naturally occurring variations remains a significant concern. In this work, we investigate the vulnerability of state-of-the-art vision models—both Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers—to small, realistic changes in 3D perspective and lighting conditions that remain within the distribution of natural images. Using a carefully controlled experimental framework, we generate perturbed images that preserve semantic content while modifying viewpoint and illumination parameters within ranges commonly encountered in real-world scenarios. Our results reveal that even minor alterations in these 3D properties can dramatically reduce model performance, with classification accuracy dropping by up to 40% in some cases, despite human observers perceiving no meaningful change in image content. Surprisingly, Vision Transformers, despite their attention-based architecture and strong performance on various vision tasks, exhibit similar fragility to these naturalistic variations as CNNs. We demonstrate that these vulnerabilities persist across model scales, architectures, and training regimes, including models trained with extensive data augmentation. Our findings highlight fundamental limitations in current vision systems' ability to build robust 3D scene understanding and suggest that architectural innovations alone may be insufficient to address these challenges without explicit modeling of 3D scene properties.

OAS-Net: Occlusion Aware Sampling Network for Accurate Optical Flow

Optical flow estimation remains challenging in regions with occlusions, where pixels visible in one frame become hidden in another. This paper introduces OAS-Net, a novel deep learning architecture that explicitly addresses occlusion handling in optical flow estimation. Our network incorporates an occlusion-aware sampling mechanism that adaptively modifies feature correlation patterns based on predicted occlusion probabilities. Unlike previous approaches that treat occluded regions as outliers or post-process them, OAS-Net integrates occlusion reasoning directly into the matching process. The network employs a dual-stream architecture with a dedicated occlusion prediction branch that guides the main flow estimation pathway. Through extensive experiments on standard benchmarks including Sintel, KITTI, and HD1K, we demonstrate that OAS-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance, with particularly significant improvements in occluded regions (reducing average endpoint error by 28% compared to leading methods). Our approach maintains computational efficiency while providing more robust flow estimates in challenging scenarios with complex object boundaries and large displacements. Code and pre-trained models are available at [project URL].

Inferring JavaScript Types Using Graph Neural Networks

Static type inference for dynamically typed languages like JavaScript has gained significant attention due to its potential to enhance code quality, improve developer productivity, and detect errors early in the development cycle. This paper presents a novel approach to JavaScript type inference using Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). We represent JavaScript programs as heterogeneous graphs that capture both syntactic structure and semantic relationships between program elements. Our model, TypeGNN, leverages this graph representation to propagate and aggregate type information across program components. The graph-based approach enables TypeGNN to capture complex contextual dependencies and non-local type constraints that traditional static analysis techniques often struggle with. We evaluate TypeGNN on a diverse corpus of JavaScript projects, demonstrating that it achieves 87% accuracy in predicting variable and function return types, outperforming existing heuristic-based and machine learning approaches by 12-18%. Furthermore, we show that TypeGNN can effectively generalize to unseen codebases and is robust to various code transformations. Our work demonstrates the potential of combining program analysis with deep learning techniques for addressing challenging problems in programming language tooling and developer assistance.

DELP-DAR System for License Plate Detection and Recognition

This paper presents DELP-DAR (Deep Enhanced License Plate Detection and Recognition), a novel end-to-end system for automatic license plate detection and recognition in complex urban environments. The proposed system employs a two-stage architecture that combines a modified YOLOv5 detection network with an attention-based recognition module to achieve robust performance across diverse lighting conditions, viewing angles, and occlusions. DELP-DAR introduces several key innovations, including a spatial transformer network for perspective correction, a multi-scale feature fusion mechanism to handle varying plate sizes, and an adaptive character segmentation approach that accommodates different license plate formats. Extensive evaluation on multiple public datasets (CCPD, AOLP, and our newly introduced ULPR dataset) demonstrates that DELP-DAR achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with detection rates of 98.7% and character recognition rates of 97.3%, while maintaining real-time performance at 35 frames per second on standard GPU hardware. The system's robustness to environmental variations and computational efficiency make it particularly suitable for intelligent transportation systems, smart parking, and law enforcement applications.

Learning High-level Prior with Convolutional Neural Networks for Semantic Segmentation

This paper presents a novel approach for incorporating high-level contextual priors into convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for semantic segmentation tasks. While CNNs have demonstrated remarkable performance in pixel-wise classification, they often struggle to capture global scene context and long-range dependencies that are crucial for accurate semantic understanding. We propose a hierarchical architecture that learns high-level semantic priors directly from data, eliminating the need for hand-crafted features or post-processing steps. Our method introduces a context-aware module that aggregates multi-scale information and models spatial relationships between semantic categories. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets including PASCAL VOC 2012, Cityscapes, and ADE20K demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms existing methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance with mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) improvements of 3.2%, 2.7%, and 2.5% respectively. The learned high-level priors prove particularly effective for segmenting objects with complex boundaries and handling cases with significant occlusion. Our approach maintains computational efficiency while substantially improving segmentation accuracy, making it suitable for real-time applications.

HoHoNet: 360 Indoor Holistic Understanding with Latent Horizontal Features

This paper presents HoHoNet, a novel neural architecture designed for holistic understanding of indoor environments from 360° panoramic images. Unlike conventional approaches that process equirectangular projections with standard 2D convolutions, our method leverages the unique horizontal patterns inherent in indoor panoramas by introducing latent horizontal features. These compact yet information-rich representations efficiently capture the full horizontal field of view while preserving spatial relationships critical for indoor scene understanding. HoHoNet employs a specialized encoder-decoder framework that first extracts these latent horizontal features and then decodes them for multiple indoor understanding tasks, including layout estimation, depth prediction, semantic segmentation, and object detection. Through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets such as Matterport3D, Stanford2D3D, and ZInD, we demonstrate that our approach not only achieves state-of-the-art performance across these tasks but also offers significant computational efficiency with reduced parameter count and inference time compared to existing methods. The horizontal feature representation enables effective multi-task learning and better generalization to unseen environments. Our work provides a unified framework for comprehensive indoor scene understanding from 360° imagery, with promising applications in virtual reality, robotics, and architectural modeling.

Reinforcement Learning for Molecular Design Guided by Quantum Mechanics

This work presents a novel framework integrating reinforcement learning (RL) with quantum mechanical (QM) principles for de novo molecular design. We develop a computational approach where an RL agent explores chemical space by sequentially constructing molecules while being guided by QM-derived rewards that capture fundamental electronic structure properties. Our architecture employs a graph-based molecular representation coupled with a policy network that learns to propose chemically valid structural modifications optimized toward desired quantum mechanical properties including HOMO-LUMO gaps, dipole moments, and formation energies. Unlike traditional virtual screening approaches, our method actively learns design principles during exploration, enabling the discovery of molecules with tailored quantum properties without relying on predefined libraries. Benchmarking against existing generative models demonstrates that our QM-guided RL approach produces molecules with superior quantum properties while maintaining synthetic accessibility. Case studies in photovoltaic material design and drug discovery highlight the framework's versatility. This integration of reinforcement learning with quantum mechanics provides a promising direction for accelerating the discovery of functional molecules with targeted electronic properties for applications in materials science and medicinal chemistry.

One Million Scenes for Autonomous Driving: ONCE Dataset

We present the ONCE (One millioN sCEnes) dataset, a large-scale, diverse collection of autonomous driving scenes designed to advance perception systems for self-driving vehicles. Comprising one million meticulously annotated driving scenarios captured across various urban and highway environments, weather conditions, and times of day, ONCE represents a significant contribution to autonomous driving research. The dataset features high-resolution sensor data from multiple modalities including LiDAR, cameras, and radar, synchronized with precise 3D bounding box annotations for vehicles, pedestrians, cyclists, and other road users. Unlike existing datasets, ONCE's unprecedented scale enables more effective training of deep learning models that can generalize across diverse driving conditions. Our benchmark evaluations demonstrate that models trained on ONCE achieve superior performance on perception tasks including 3D object detection, tracking, and segmentation compared to those trained on smaller datasets. We believe ONCE will serve as a valuable resource for the research community and accelerate progress toward safer and more reliable autonomous driving systems.

Reverse-engineering Bar Charts Using Neural Networks

This paper presents a novel approach to automatically extract quantitative data from bar chart images using deep neural networks. While bar charts are designed to communicate data visually, recovering the precise underlying values poses significant challenges for automated systems. We propose a multi-stage neural architecture that combines computer vision techniques with specialized regression components to accurately reverse-engineer bar charts. Our model first employs a convolutional neural network to detect and segment individual bars, followed by a calibration network that interprets axis scales and maps visual heights to numerical values. Tested on a diverse dataset of 5,000 bar charts spanning various styles, colors, and orientations, our system achieves a mean absolute percentage error of 2.3%, significantly outperforming previous methods. We demonstrate practical applications in data extraction from scientific literature, financial reports, and legacy documents. This work represents an important step toward automated chart understanding and data recovery, with potential applications in digital archiving, meta-analysis, and data reuse.

Learning 3D-aware Egocentric Spatial-Temporal Interaction via Graph Convolutional Networks

This paper introduces a novel approach for understanding human-object interactions from egocentric perspectives by incorporating 3D spatial awareness through graph convolutional networks (GCNs). While existing methods for egocentric action recognition often rely on 2D visual features, they frequently struggle to capture the complex spatial relationships and temporal dynamics that characterize natural human interactions with objects. Our proposed framework represents the egocentric scene as a dynamic graph structure where nodes correspond to detected objects and hands, while edges encode their 3D spatial relationships and temporal evolution. By leveraging depth estimation and pose tracking, we construct 3D-aware spatial-temporal graphs that preserve the geometric configuration of interactions. Our multi-stream GCN architecture processes these representations to learn both short and long-range dependencies across the interaction sequence. Extensive experiments on standard egocentric datasets (EPIC-KITCHENS, EGO4D) demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving 6.2% improvement in action recognition accuracy and 8.7% in anticipation tasks. Ablation studies confirm that the explicit modeling of 3D spatial relationships and temporal dynamics provides crucial information for understanding egocentric interactions. The proposed framework offers promising directions for applications in augmented reality, robotics, and assistive technologies where understanding natural human-object interactions from first-person viewpoints is essential.

Temporal Attention-Augmented Graph Convolutional Network for Efficient Skeleton-Based Human Action Recognition

This paper presents a novel approach to skeleton-based human action recognition through the introduction of a Temporal Attention-Augmented Graph Convolutional Network (TA-GCN). While existing graph convolutional networks effectively model spatial relationships in skeleton data, they often inadequately capture the temporal dynamics crucial for action recognition. Our proposed TA-GCN architecture addresses this limitation by integrating a specialized temporal attention mechanism that dynamically weighs the importance of different time frames during action sequences. This mechanism enables the network to focus on the most discriminative temporal segments while maintaining computational efficiency. We employ a hierarchical feature extraction strategy where spatial features are first extracted using graph convolutions on individual skeleton frames, followed by our temporal attention module that learns interdependencies across the temporal dimension. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets including NTU RGB+D, Kinetics-Skeleton, and Northwestern-UCLA demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance while requiring significantly fewer parameters and less computational resources than existing methods. Additionally, ablation studies verify the effectiveness of each component in our proposed architecture. The TA-GCN framework presents a balanced solution for real-time human action recognition applications where both accuracy and computational efficiency are essential.

Seeing Colors: Learning Semantic Text Encoding for Classification

This paper introduces a novel approach to text classification through a semantic color encoding framework that bridges natural language understanding and visual representation learning. Our method, Semantic Color Encoding (SCE), transforms textual features into a color-based representation space where semantic relationships are preserved through carefully calibrated color mappings. By encoding linguistic features as color vectors, we enable models to leverage both the discriminative power of traditional NLP techniques and the spatial pattern recognition capabilities of vision-based architectures. Experiments across multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that SCE outperforms traditional text classification approaches by 4.7% on average, with particularly strong performance on tasks requiring fine-grained semantic distinction. The approach shows remarkable data efficiency, requiring 35% less training data to achieve comparable performance to baseline methods. Our analysis reveals that the color-encoded representations form intuitive clusters that align with human semantic intuitions, suggesting that this cross-modal approach captures fundamental aspects of meaning organization. These findings highlight the potential of synergistic text-to-color mappings as a powerful tool for classification tasks across domains including sentiment analysis, topic categorization, and intent recognition.

Lightweight Mask R-CNN for Long-Range Wireless Power Transfer Systems

This paper presents a lightweight adaptation of Mask R-CNN designed specifically for object detection and instance segmentation in long-range wireless power transfer (WPT) systems. The proposed architecture addresses the computational constraints of WPT receivers while maintaining detection accuracy necessary for optimal power delivery. By implementing depth-wise separable convolutions and an efficient feature pyramid network, we reduced the model size by 73% and inference time by 68% compared to standard Mask R-CNN implementations, with only a 4.2% decrease in mean Average Precision (mAP). Our approach enables real-time detection of power-receiving devices at distances up to 15 meters, allowing for precise targeting of wireless power beams. Experimental results demonstrate that the lightweight model successfully operates within the energy and computational constraints of WPT systems while achieving 92.7% charging efficiency compared to perfect alignment scenarios. This work represents a significant advancement in making computer vision-guided WPT systems practical for consumer applications, particularly in smart homes and office environments.

Strong-Weak Distribution Alignment for Adaptive Object Detection

Domain adaptation for object detection remains challenging due to the significant distribution shifts between source (strong) and target (weak) domains. This paper introduces Strong-Weak Distribution Alignment (SWDA), a novel framework that addresses the fundamental challenges in adaptive object detection. Our approach simultaneously aligns feature distributions at both image and instance levels while preserving the discriminative power needed for accurate detection. SWDA employs a multi-stage alignment strategy that progressively reduces domain discrepancy through: (1) a domain-adversarial learning mechanism with gradient reversal to align global image representations, (2) a region proposal adaptation module that refines instance-level features, and (3) a consistency regularization component that enforces prediction stability across domains. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets including Cityscapes, Foggy Cityscapes, KITTI, and BDD100K demonstrate that SWDA significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving 4.3% higher mAP on challenging cross-domain scenarios while maintaining computational efficiency during inference. Our approach proves particularly effective when domain shifts involve weather conditions, lighting variations, and camera perspectives, making it valuable for real-world applications like autonomous driving and surveillance systems.

Incremental Few-Shot Learning with Attention Attractor Networks

This paper introduces Attention Attractor Networks (AANs), a novel approach to address the challenging problem of incremental few-shot learning. While deep neural networks have achieved remarkable performance in various domains, they typically require large amounts of labeled data and struggle with continually learning new concepts from limited examples without catastrophically forgetting previously acquired knowledge. Our proposed AAN framework leverages a dynamic attention mechanism that creates "attractor points" in the representation space, effectively guiding the model to preserve critical information about previously learned classes while accommodating new ones. By incorporating a meta-learning strategy, our model learns how to efficiently adapt to new tasks with minimal examples. Extensive experiments on standard few-shot learning benchmarks including miniImageNet, tieredImageNet, and CUB-200 demonstrate that AANs significantly outperform existing methods in incremental few-shot scenarios, reducing forgetting by an average of 21.3% while improving new class adaptation by 15.7%. Additionally, our approach requires minimal computational overhead during inference, making it practical for real-world applications. The proposed architecture provides a promising direction for developing systems capable of continuous learning in data-constrained environments.

A Novel Attention-based Aggregation Function to Combine Vision and Language

This paper introduces a novel attention-based aggregation function designed to effectively combine visual and linguistic information in multimodal systems. While existing approaches often rely on simple concatenation or fixed weighting schemes to merge these modalities, our method dynamically determines the importance of each modality based on the specific input context. We propose a cross-modal attention mechanism that learns to identify and emphasize the most relevant features across both domains, enabling more nuanced integration of visual cues and linguistic semantics. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets including VQA, image captioning, and visual grounding tasks demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms traditional fusion methods, achieving state-of-the-art results with 4-6% improvement across metrics. Further analysis reveals that our model exhibits adaptive behavior, appropriately shifting attention between modalities depending on the nature of the task and input. The proposed aggregation function provides a flexible framework that can be readily incorporated into various multimodal architectures, offering a promising direction for advancing vision-language integration in artificial intelligence systems.

Self-supervised Monocular Depth Estimation for All Day Images using Domain Separation

Monocular depth estimation in diverse lighting conditions remains a significant challenge for autonomous driving and robotics applications. This paper presents a novel self-supervised learning framework for monocular depth estimation that effectively handles images captured across various times of day without requiring ground truth depth annotations. Our key contribution is a domain separation approach that disentangles illumination-variant and illumination-invariant features within the network architecture. By introducing a dedicated illumination adaptation module and a consistency regularization mechanism, our model learns to extract geometric structure independent of lighting conditions while maintaining performance across domains. Extensive experiments on the Oxford RobotCar and KITTI datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art self-supervised methods by up to 15% on standard metrics when tested on challenging dawn, dusk, and night sequences. Additionally, our domain separation strategy enables effective knowledge transfer between different illumination conditions, reducing the performance gap between daytime and nighttime scenarios. The proposed method provides a robust solution for real-world applications requiring reliable depth estimation regardless of lighting conditions, without the prohibitive cost of collecting annotated data across all possible environmental variations.

Abstract: Generative Transition Mechanism to Image-to-Image Translation via Encoded Transformation

This paper introduces a novel generative transition mechanism for image-to-image translation that leverages encoded transformations to overcome limitations in existing approaches. Our method, which we call Encoded Transformation Network (ETNet), employs a dual-pathway architecture that separates content preservation and style transformation, allowing for more precise control over the translation process. By encoding the transformation parameters in a latent space, ETNet can generate smooth transitions between source and target domains while preserving structural integrity. We demonstrate that our approach significantly reduces artifacts common in traditional GAN-based translation methods, particularly in challenging scenarios involving large domain gaps. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets show that ETNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both qualitative visual fidelity and quantitative metrics, including FID and LPIPS scores. Additionally, our model demonstrates improved disentanglement capabilities and enhanced interpretability of the transformation process. The proposed mechanism not only advances the field of image-to-image translation but also provides insights into the design of more effective generative models for visual content manipulation.

SVT-Net: Super Light-Weight Sparse Voxel Transformer for Large Scale Place Recognition

This paper introduces SVT-Net, a novel super light-weight transformer-based architecture designed specifically for large-scale place recognition using 3D point cloud data. While existing methods often struggle with computational efficiency when processing sparse 3D data, our proposed Sparse Voxel Transformer network leverages a voxelized representation combined with an efficient attention mechanism that operates only on non-empty voxels. SVT-Net significantly reduces computational overhead while maintaining high discriminative power for place recognition tasks. Our architecture incorporates a hierarchical feature extraction pipeline with sparse convolutions followed by transformer blocks that capture global contextual relationships between spatially distant features. Extensive evaluations on benchmark datasets including Oxford RobotCar, KITTI, and Mulran demonstrate that SVT-Net achieves state-of-the-art place recognition performance with substantially lower computational requirements (75% fewer parameters and 68% less inference time) compared to existing methods. Furthermore, SVT-Net shows remarkable robustness to environmental changes, viewpoint variations, and sensor noise, making it particularly suitable for deployment in resource-constrained platforms for real-world autonomous navigation applications. The code and pre-trained models are made publicly available to facilitate further research in this direction.

Two Layer Ensemble of Deep Learning Models for Medical Image Segmentation

This paper presents a novel two-layer ensemble approach for medical image segmentation that combines multiple deep learning architectures to improve segmentation accuracy and robustness. Our method integrates diverse state-of-the-art segmentation models in a hierarchical framework, where the first layer consists of individual deep learning models such as U-Net, SegNet, DeepLab, and attention-based architectures trained independently on medical imaging datasets. The second layer employs a meta-learning strategy that optimizes the fusion of predictions from the first-layer models using a trainable weighting mechanism that adapts to different anatomical structures and imaging modalities. Experiments conducted on multiple public datasets, including brain MRI, abdominal CT, and histopathology images, demonstrate that our two-layer ensemble consistently outperforms individual models and traditional ensemble methods, achieving improvements of 4-7% in Dice similarity coefficient and 3-5% in Hausdorff distance. Furthermore, the proposed approach shows enhanced generalization to unseen data and increased resilience to dataset variability. These results suggest that our hierarchical ensemble framework effectively leverages the complementary strengths of different segmentation architectures, making it particularly valuable for challenging medical image segmentation tasks with limited training data or high anatomical variability.

Structural Compression of Convolutional Neural Networks

This paper presents a novel approach for compressing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) through structural optimization while maintaining performance. We introduce a hierarchical compression framework that systematically reduces model complexity by targeting redundancies at multiple structural levels. Our method combines filter pruning, channel reduction, and architectural restructuring to achieve significant compression ratios without substantial accuracy degradation. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach reduces model size by up to 85% and computational requirements by 73% while maintaining accuracy within 1.5% of the original networks. For resource-constrained deployment scenarios, we further propose an adaptive compression scheme that dynamically balances model size and accuracy based on specific hardware constraints. Comparative analysis shows our method outperforms existing compression techniques in terms of the compression-accuracy trade-off. These results highlight the potential of structural compression for deploying deep learning models in resource-limited environments such as mobile and edge devices.

Two-Stream Appearance Transfer Network for Person Image Generation

This paper introduces a novel approach to person image generation through the Two-Stream Appearance Transfer Network (TSAT-Net), which addresses the challenging task of synthesizing realistic person images with arbitrary poses while preserving appearance details. Unlike previous methods that struggle with spatial misalignment between source and target poses, our network employs a dual-stream architecture that effectively decouples and recombines appearance and structural information. The first stream extracts comprehensive appearance features from the source image, while the second stream generates structural guidance based on the target pose. Our key innovation lies in the appearance transfer module that adaptively maps source appearance features to the target pose space through a learned warping mechanism, enabling precise detail preservation even under extreme pose variations. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets including DeepFashion and Market-1501 demonstrate that TSAT-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both visual quality and identity preservation. Quantitative evaluations show significant improvements in FID, SSIM, and LPIPS metrics compared to existing approaches. The proposed method exhibits robust performance across diverse scenarios, including challenging cases with occlusions, complex garments, and dramatic pose differences, making it applicable for virtual try-on, video synthesis, and data augmentation for person re-identification.

A Kernel to Exploit Informative Missingness in Multivariate Time Series from EHRs

Electronic Health Records (EHRs) contain rich multivariate time series data that offer valuable insights for clinical prediction tasks. However, these time series frequently contain missing values that pose significant challenges for traditional machine learning approaches. In this work, we propose a novel kernel method specifically designed to leverage the informative nature of missingness patterns in EHR data. Unlike conventional approaches that treat missing values as nuisances to be imputed or ignored, our kernel explicitly models the information contained in the missingness patterns themselves. We develop a theoretically grounded kernel framework that captures both the observed values and the temporal patterns of observations/non-observations across multiple clinical variables. Through extensive experiments on real-world EHR datasets spanning diverse clinical prediction tasks, including mortality prediction, hospital readmission, and disease onset, we demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods for handling missing data in time series. Our kernel achieves an average improvement of 12% in AUROC across tasks compared to conventional imputation methods. Furthermore, we show that the learned kernel representations provide interpretable insights into clinically meaningful patterns of missing measurements. This work establishes a new paradigm for modeling multivariate clinical time series that transforms the challenge of missing data into an opportunity for enhanced predictive performance.

Efficient Reinforcement Learning in Resource Allocation Problems Through Permutation Invariant Multi-task Learning

Resource allocation problems are ubiquitous across domains including cloud computing, logistics, and wireless communications. These problems are characterized by the need to efficiently distribute limited resources among competing demands, often under uncertainty and dynamic conditions. This paper introduces a novel reinforcement learning approach that exploits the inherent permutation invariance of resource allocation problems to achieve sample-efficient learning. Our key contribution is a permutation invariant multi-task learning framework that enables knowledge transfer across different problem instances, significantly reducing the training data requirements. By leveraging deep set architectures and attention mechanisms, our approach learns representations that are invariant to the ordering of resources and tasks, while capturing the essential structure of allocation problems. Experimental results across diverse domains demonstrate that our method achieves 30-50% faster convergence and 15-25% better performance compared to standard reinforcement learning approaches. Furthermore, we show that our trained models generalize effectively to previously unseen problem instances with varying numbers of resources and tasks. This work provides a promising direction for addressing complex resource allocation challenges in real-world systems where data efficiency and adaptability are critical.

Attribution Mask: Filtering Out Irrelevant Features By Recursively Focusing Attention on Inputs of DNNs

Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have demonstrated remarkable performance across various tasks, yet their black-box nature poses significant challenges for interpretability and trustworthiness. This paper introduces Attribution Mask, a novel approach that recursively filters irrelevant features from input data by leveraging attention mechanisms. Our method systematically identifies and masks out input features that minimally contribute to model predictions, thereby revealing the essential components driving DNN decisions. Through an iterative process, Attribution Mask progressively refines the input representation until only the most salient features remain. Extensive experiments across image classification, natural language processing, and time series analysis demonstrate that our approach not only enhances model interpretability but also improves robustness against adversarial attacks and noisy inputs. Quantitative evaluations show that Attribution Mask outperforms existing attribution methods in terms of faithfulness to model predictions and localization of discriminative features. Furthermore, we show that the masks generated by our approach can be utilized as regularizers during training to encourage models to focus on semantically meaningful patterns. Our work contributes a generalizable framework for understanding DNN behavior and provides practitioners with a tool to build more transparent and reliable AI systems.

Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolution for Resting-State fMRI Analysis

Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) provides valuable insights into intrinsic brain connectivity patterns during the absence of task performance. However, effectively modeling the complex spatio-temporal dynamics of brain activity remains challenging. This paper introduces a novel approach utilizing spatio-temporal graph convolutional networks (ST-GCN) for analyzing rs-fMRI data. Our method represents brain regions as nodes in a graph, with edges defined by both anatomical connections and functional correlations. The proposed ST-GCN framework simultaneously captures spatial dependencies between brain regions and temporal evolution of neural signals through specialized graph convolution operations across both dimensions. We evaluate our approach on multiple rs-fMRI datasets, demonstrating superior performance compared to traditional methods in functional connectivity analysis, brain state classification, and identification of neurological disorders. Results show that our model achieves 15% higher accuracy in distinguishing patients with neurological conditions from healthy controls while providing interpretable visualization of discriminative spatio-temporal patterns. This work advances rs-fMRI analysis by effectively leveraging the inherent graph structure of brain networks while accounting for their dynamic temporal characteristics, offering new opportunities for understanding brain organization and dysfunction.

Airbnb Price Prediction Using Machine Learning and Sentiment Analysis

This study presents a novel approach to Airbnb price prediction by combining traditional machine learning techniques with sentiment analysis of customer reviews. While conventional pricing models typically rely on quantitative features such as location, property size, and amenities, they often overlook the qualitative aspects embedded in guest feedback. Our research integrates these textual insights to enhance prediction accuracy. We collected data from over 10,000 Airbnb listings across major metropolitan areas, extracting both structured attributes and unstructured review text. The methodology employs a two-stage model: first, a natural language processing pipeline analyzes review sentiment, extracting key opinion factors; second, these sentiment features are combined with traditional property attributes in ensemble machine learning algorithms (Random Forest, XGBoost, and neural networks). Results demonstrate that the integrated model achieves a 17.3% improvement in prediction accuracy compared to baseline models using only conventional features. Particularly, sentiment factors related to cleanliness, host communication, and perceived value showed strong correlations with price variations. This research provides valuable insights for hosts in optimizing pricing strategies and for the platform in improving recommendation systems, while contributing to the growing field of hybrid approaches in predictive analytics for sharing economy platforms.

Deep Generative Model for Sparse Graphs using Text-Based Learning with Augmentation in Generative Examination Networks

This paper introduces a novel framework for generating sparse graph structures by leveraging text-based learning approaches within Generative Examination Networks (GENs). While existing graph generative models often struggle with the inherent sparsity and complex topological features of real-world networks, our approach addresses these limitations through a text-augmented learning paradigm. By encoding graph structures as textual representations and employing large language models to learn the underlying distributions, we enable more effective modeling of sparse connectivity patterns. Our method incorporates a specialized augmentation technique that enhances the diversity and quality of generated graphs while preserving their sparsity characteristics. Experimental evaluations across multiple domains, including social networks, molecular structures, and knowledge graphs, demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of graph validity, novelty, and adherence to domain-specific constraints. The proposed framework not only advances the capabilities of graph generative models but also establishes a promising direction for cross-modal learning between textual and structural data representations.

SSIMLayer: Towards Robust Deep Representation Learning via Nonlinear Structural Similarity

Deep neural networks have demonstrated remarkable success in representation learning, yet they remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks and distribution shifts. In this paper, we introduce SSIMLayer, a novel architectural component that enhances the robustness of deep representation learning by incorporating nonlinear structural similarity metrics into the network's feature extraction process. Unlike conventional approaches that rely solely on pixel-wise or feature-wise distances, SSIMLayer captures local structural information by modeling the complex interdependencies between neighboring features. Our method extends the traditional Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) to high-dimensional feature spaces through learnable nonlinear transformations that adapt to the underlying data distribution. Experimental results across multiple vision tasks demonstrate that networks equipped with SSIMLayer exhibit significantly improved robustness against adversarial perturbations (up to 17.8% higher accuracy) and natural distribution shifts (12.3% performance gain) compared to baseline architectures, while maintaining competitive performance on clean data. Further analysis reveals that SSIMLayer promotes the emergence of more semantically meaningful feature representations that better preserve structural information critical for generalization. Our approach requires minimal computational overhead and can be seamlessly integrated into existing deep learning frameworks, offering a practical solution for enhancing model robustness in real-world applications.

Wide-minima Density Hypothesis and the Explore-Exploit Learning Rate Schedule

This paper introduces the Wide-minima Density Hypothesis (WDH), which posits that wide minima in neural network loss landscapes are not randomly distributed but tend to cluster in specific regions. Building on this hypothesis, we propose a novel learning rate schedule, the Explore-Exploit Learning Rate Schedule (EELRS), which systematically transitions from exploration to exploitation during training. In the exploration phase, higher learning rates allow the optimization process to traverse barriers between different basins, increasing the probability of discovering regions dense with wide minima. The exploitation phase then employs progressively smaller learning rates to settle into the most favorable wide minimum. Through extensive empirical evaluation on image classification, natural language processing, and reinforcement learning tasks, we demonstrate that EELRS consistently outperforms traditional learning rate schedules, including step decay, cosine annealing, and cyclical schedules. Theoretical analysis connects our approach to concepts from statistical physics and Bayesian optimization, providing insights into why preferentially sampling from regions with high densities of wide minima leads to superior generalization. Our findings suggest that the geometric distribution of minima in loss landscapes is a crucial factor in developing effective optimization strategies for deep neural networks.

Dual Adaptive Pyramid Network for Cross-Stain Histopathology Image Segmentation

Histopathology image segmentation is crucial for cancer diagnosis and treatment planning, but faces significant challenges due to staining variations across medical institutions. This paper introduces the Dual Adaptive Pyramid Network (DAPNet), a novel architecture designed specifically for cross-stain histopathology image segmentation. Our approach leverages a dual-stream pyramid structure that processes multi-scale features while adaptively adjusting to stain variations. The network consists of a stain-invariant feature extraction pathway that captures morphological structures independent of staining properties, and a stain-adaptive pathway that learns to normalize different staining protocols. These pathways are integrated through an attention-based fusion module that dynamically balances the contribution of each stream based on staining characteristics. Extensive experiments on multi-institutional datasets spanning H&E, IHC, and special stains demonstrate that DAPNet significantly outperforms existing methods, achieving a 12.3% improvement in Dice coefficient and 9.8% reduction in Hausdorff distance compared to state-of-the-art approaches. Additionally, our ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of each component in handling stain variability. The proposed DAPNet provides a robust solution for cross-stain histopathology image segmentation that can be readily integrated into clinical workflows across different institutions without requiring stain-specific retraining.

CNN-based Segmentation of Medical Imaging Data

This paper presents a comprehensive exploration of convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures for segmentation tasks in medical imaging data. We investigate the application of deep learning techniques across multiple imaging modalities including MRI, CT, ultrasound, and X-ray images. Our approach leverages recent advances in CNN architectures, particularly U-Net and its variants, to address the unique challenges of medical image segmentation such as limited annotated data, class imbalance, and the need for high precision in organ and pathology boundary delineation. We evaluate several optimization strategies including transfer learning, data augmentation, and specialized loss functions designed to enhance segmentation accuracy in low-contrast regions. Experiments conducted on publicly available datasets demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves state-of-the-art performance with Dice similarity coefficients exceeding 0.85 across multiple anatomical structures and pathologies. Additionally, we present an ablation study highlighting the contribution of each architectural component to overall performance. The proposed methods show potential for clinical translation by reducing manual segmentation workload while maintaining high accuracy, potentially accelerating diagnosis and treatment planning workflows.

FiGLearn: Filter and Graph Learning using Optimal Transport

This paper introduces FiGLearn, a novel framework that unifies filter and graph learning through the lens of optimal transport theory. While traditional graph signal processing approaches typically assume a fixed graph structure, real-world networks often exhibit dynamic topologies that evolve over time. FiGLearn addresses this limitation by simultaneously learning both the underlying graph structure and the optimal graph filters from observed data. Our approach formulates the joint optimization problem as an optimal transport task, where the graph topology serves as the transport plan between signal distributions. We derive theoretical guarantees for the convergence of our algorithm and establish bounds on the reconstruction error. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including traffic networks, brain connectivity graphs, and social media interaction data, demonstrate that FiGLearn consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of prediction accuracy and structural fidelity. The framework shows particular promise in scenarios with incomplete or noisy observations, where the ability to adapt both filter and graph parameters provides significant advantages. Our results highlight the potential of optimal transport theory as a powerful tool for graph representation learning in dynamic environments.

Dueling Deep Q-Network for Unsupervised Inter-frame Eye Movement Correction in Optical Coherence Tomography Volumes

Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) is a non-invasive imaging technique widely used in ophthalmology for diagnosing and monitoring retinal diseases. However, involuntary eye movements during image acquisition cause misalignment between consecutive B-scans, resulting in distorted volumetric reconstructions that can impair clinical interpretation. This paper presents a novel unsupervised approach for inter-frame eye movement correction in OCT volumes using a Dueling Deep Q-Network (DDQN) reinforcement learning framework. Our method formulates the alignment problem as a sequential decision-making process, where the DDQN learns to predict optimal rigid transformations between adjacent B-scans without requiring manually aligned ground truth data. The dueling architecture, which decouples state value and advantage estimation, enables more stable and efficient learning of the correction policy. We introduce a composite reward function that combines structural similarity metrics and anatomical continuity constraints to guide the alignment process. Experiments conducted on 150 OCT volumes from both healthy subjects and patients with various retinal pathologies demonstrate that our approach achieves superior correction accuracy compared to conventional registration methods and previous deep learning approaches, with a mean registration error of 3.2±0.8 μm. Furthermore, the corrected volumes show improved visualization of retinal layers and enhanced performance in downstream tasks such as layer segmentation and pathology detection. Our unsupervised DDQN framework represents a significant advancement in OCT image processing, potentially improving clinical diagnosis and treatment planning in ophthalmology.

Diffusion-based Deep Active Learning

Active learning strategies aim to minimize annotation costs by intelligently selecting the most informative samples for labeling. While these approaches have shown promise in traditional machine learning settings, their application to deep learning models presents unique challenges due to model complexity and data dimensionality. This paper introduces Diffusion-based Deep Active Learning (DDAL), a novel framework that leverages generative diffusion models to guide the sample selection process. Our approach utilizes the learned latent representations of diffusion models to identify uncertain, diverse, and representative samples from unlabeled pools. By modeling the probability flows in the feature space, DDAL effectively captures both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty, leading to more informed acquisition decisions. We empirically evaluate DDAL across multiple vision and language benchmarks, demonstrating consistent improvements over state-of-the-art active learning methods. Our experiments show that DDAL reduces labeling requirements by up to 40% while maintaining comparable performance to fully-supervised baselines. Furthermore, we provide theoretical insights into why diffusion models are particularly well-suited for active learning scenarios. This work establishes a promising direction for combining generative modeling with active learning to address the data efficiency challenges in deep learning.

Automatic System for Counting Cells with Elliptical Shape

This paper presents a novel automated system for accurately detecting and counting elliptical-shaped cells in microscopic images. The proposed method addresses the significant challenges in cell quantification, including cell clustering, variable morphology, and image quality inconsistencies. Our approach combines adaptive image preprocessing techniques with an elliptical feature extraction algorithm that leverages both geometric and intensity-based parameters. The system employs a two-stage process: initial segmentation using adaptive thresholding followed by ellipse fitting with a modified Hough transform optimized for biological samples. Validation experiments conducted on diverse cell populations, including lymphocytes, erythrocytes, and epithelial cells, demonstrated a counting accuracy of 94.7% compared to manual counts, with significantly reduced processing time. The system successfully differentiated between overlapping cells and was robust against varying illumination conditions. This tool provides researchers and clinicians with an efficient and reliable method for cell quantification, with potential applications in hematology, oncology, and microbiology. The developed software is available as an open-source platform that can be readily integrated into existing laboratory workflows.

An Adaptive Fuzzy-Based System to Simulate, Quantify and Compensate Color Blindness

This paper presents a novel adaptive fuzzy-based system designed to address the challenges faced by individuals with color vision deficiency (CVD). Our approach integrates three critical functionalities: simulation, quantification, and compensation of color blindness. The system employs fuzzy logic principles to handle the inherent uncertainties in color perception and to adapt to individual variations in CVD. First, we develop accurate simulation models that render images as perceived by individuals with different types and severities of color blindness. Second, we introduce a quantification framework that assesses the degree of color vision impairment through a series of calibrated tests, producing a personalized color deficiency profile. Finally, we implement an adaptive compensation mechanism that dynamically adjusts color representations in digital content to enhance color discriminability for CVD individuals. Experimental evaluation with 127 participants (83 with various forms of CVD and 44 with normal color vision) demonstrates that our system achieves a 78% improvement in color distinction tasks and a 65% enhancement in user experience compared to existing approaches. The proposed system offers significant potential for applications in accessibility technology, digital content creation, and assistive devices, providing a comprehensive solution to improve the visual experience of individuals with color blindness.

Removing Rain Streaks by a Linear Model

This paper introduces a novel approach to rain streak removal from single images using a linear decomposition model. Rain streaks in images present significant challenges for computer vision applications, degrading visual quality and hindering downstream tasks such as object detection and scene understanding. Our proposed method models rain-affected images as a linear superposition of a clean background layer and a rain streak layer, allowing for effective separation through optimization techniques. We formulate the rain removal problem as a constrained minimization task that leverages the distinct characteristics of rain streaks—their sparsity, directionality, and high-frequency components—while preserving the structural integrity of the background image. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world rainy images demonstrate that our linear model outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both quantitative metrics (PSNR, SSIM) and visual quality assessment. The proposed approach achieves superior rain streak removal while maintaining computational efficiency, making it suitable for real-time applications. Furthermore, we provide a comprehensive analysis of parameter sensitivity and model limitations to guide future research directions in this domain.

Second-Moment Loss: A Novel Regression Objective for Improved Uncertainties

Standard regression approaches often provide point estimates without reliable uncertainty quantification, limiting their utility in high-stakes applications. This paper introduces the Second-Moment Loss (SML), a novel regression objective function designed to simultaneously optimize prediction accuracy and uncertainty estimation. Unlike conventional methods that treat uncertainty as a secondary consideration, SML directly incorporates variance estimation into the primary optimization objective by modeling the second moment of the prediction error distribution. Through theoretical analysis, we demonstrate that SML converges to optimal uncertainty estimates under mild assumptions. Our extensive empirical evaluation across diverse datasets—including medical diagnostics, financial forecasting, and environmental modeling—shows that models trained with SML consistently provide better-calibrated uncertainty estimates compared to traditional approaches like Mean Squared Error with post-hoc uncertainty quantification. Additionally, SML-trained models demonstrate improved robustness to distribution shifts and outliers while maintaining competitive accuracy. The proposed method requires minimal modifications to existing deep learning architectures and introduces negligible computational overhead during training. These results suggest that SML represents a promising approach for applications where reliable uncertainty quantification is as important as predictive accuracy.

CNN-based Temporal Super Resolution of Radar Rainfall Products

This study proposes a novel approach to enhance the temporal resolution of radar rainfall products using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Radar-based precipitation estimates are crucial for hydrological applications, but their usefulness is often limited by insufficient temporal resolution. We developed a deep learning framework that generates intermediate rainfall frames between consecutive radar observations, effectively increasing temporal resolution without requiring additional sensor deployment. Our CNN architecture employs a U-Net-based design with residual connections and attention mechanisms to capture the complex spatiotemporal dynamics of precipitation systems. The model was trained on a diverse dataset comprising 5-minute radar rainfall composites from multiple weather radar networks, spanning different climate regions and precipitation types. Evaluation results demonstrate that our approach outperforms traditional interpolation methods and physics-based advection models, reducing RMSE by 37% and improving structural similarity metrics by 42%. The enhanced temporal resolution enables more accurate rainfall intensity estimations during convective events and improves the detection of rapidly evolving precipitation systems. This methodology shows promise for operational implementation in flood forecasting, urban hydrology, and nowcasting applications where high-frequency rainfall information is essential.

Hierarchical Generation of Molecular Graphs using Structural Motifs

Molecular graph generation represents a critical challenge in computational chemistry and drug discovery. This paper introduces a novel hierarchical approach to molecular graph generation that leverages structural motifs as building blocks. Our method decomposes the complex task of molecule generation into a two-phase process: first identifying and extracting meaningful chemical motifs from training data, then learning to assemble these motifs into chemically valid and functionally relevant molecules. By operating at multiple levels of abstraction, our approach effectively captures both local chemical patterns and global molecular structures. We implement this hierarchical framework using a combination of graph neural networks and transformer architectures, where motifs are represented as nodes in a higher-level graph and subsequently expanded into their constituent atoms and bonds. Experimental results across multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach generates molecules with improved validity, novelty, and diversity compared to atom-by-atom generation methods, while maintaining synthetic accessibility. Furthermore, when applied to property-targeted generation tasks, our motif-based approach more effectively navigates the chemical space toward desired molecular properties. This work provides a promising direction for molecular design by mimicking the hierarchical thinking patterns of medicinal chemists who conceptualize molecules as arrangements of functional groups and structural fragments.

Real-time Deep Pose Estimation with Geodesic Loss for Image-to-Template Rigid Registration

This paper presents a novel deep learning framework for real-time rigid registration between intraoperative images and preoperative templates. We address the fundamental challenges of achieving both computational efficiency and high accuracy in medical image registration by introducing a convolutional neural network architecture that directly estimates the 6-DOF rigid transformation parameters. Our key contribution is the incorporation of a geodesic loss function that respects the geometry of the SE(3) manifold of rigid transformations, leading to more stable training and improved registration accuracy compared to conventional L1/L2 losses. The proposed method achieves sub-millimeter precision and operates at over 30 frames per second on standard GPU hardware, making it suitable for time-critical clinical applications. Extensive validation on multi-modal datasets including CT, MRI, and ultrasound demonstrates that our approach outperforms traditional iterative registration algorithms and recent learning-based methods in both accuracy and speed. Furthermore, we show that our network generalizes well to unseen clinical data with varying image quality, anatomical structures, and pathologies. This work represents a significant advancement toward reliable real-time surgical navigation and image-guided interventions.

Cross-Modal Progressive Comprehension for Referring Segmentation

Referring segmentation, which aims to segment an object in an image based on a natural language expression, remains challenging due to the complex interplay between visual and linguistic modalities. In this paper, we propose a novel Cross-Modal Progressive Comprehension (CMPC) framework that addresses the limitations of existing approaches by enabling bidirectional and iterative refinement between visual and textual features. Our framework introduces a progressive comprehension mechanism that gradually builds understanding through multiple stages of cross-modal interaction. At each stage, visual features are guided by linguistic cues while textual representations are simultaneously enhanced by visual context, creating a mutually reinforcing loop. This approach allows the model to resolve ambiguities in both modalities and focus on the most relevant image regions and textual phrases. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets—RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and G-Ref—demonstrate that our CMPC framework significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving improvements of 2.3%, 2.7%, and 3.1% in IoU scores, respectively. Qualitative analysis further reveals our model's superior ability to handle complex linguistic expressions and accurately segment objects in challenging visual scenarios. Our work provides new insights into cross-modal reasoning and establishes a strong foundation for future research in referring segmentation.

ROBO: Robust, Fully Neural Object Detection for Robot Soccer

This paper presents ROBO, a novel fully neural object detection framework designed specifically for robot soccer environments. Unlike traditional computer vision approaches that rely on hand-crafted features or hybrid methods, ROBO employs an end-to-end neural architecture that demonstrates exceptional robustness across varying lighting conditions, occlusions, and camera perspectives. Our approach leverages a custom convolutional backbone with domain-specific attention mechanisms to accurately detect and localize key objects in the robot soccer domain, including the ball, field markings, goalposts, and other robots. Experimental results show that ROBO achieves state-of-the-art detection accuracy (95.7% mAP) while maintaining real-time performance (60+ FPS) on standard robot hardware. The system demonstrates remarkable generalization capabilities across multiple RoboCup leagues and significantly outperforms previous methods in challenging scenarios, reducing false positive rates by 78% under variable lighting. We also introduce a synthetic data generation pipeline that substantially reduces the annotation burden while improving model robustness. ROBO's architecture and training methodology provide valuable insights for robust perception systems in dynamic, adversarial environments beyond robot soccer.

Geometry-Guided Street-View Panorama Synthesis from Satellite Imagery

This paper introduces a novel approach for synthesizing realistic street-view panoramas using only satellite imagery as input. While satellite data offers extensive geographic coverage, the lack of corresponding ground-level perspectives limits applications in urban visualization, navigation, and virtual reality. We propose a geometry-guided framework that leverages the inherent spatial relationships between overhead and street-level viewpoints to address this challenge. Our method first extracts geometric priors from satellite imagery, including building footprints, height estimates, and road networks, to construct a coarse 3D proxy of the urban environment. This structural foundation guides a two-stage generative process: an initial panorama synthesis that respects spatial layout constraints, followed by a refinement phase that enhances visual details and maintains geometric consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing cross-view synthesis methods across multiple metrics, producing panoramas with improved structural accuracy and visual fidelity. The framework enables large-scale street-view coverage in regions where ground-level imagery is unavailable or outdated, with potential applications in urban planning, navigation systems, and immersive virtual environments.

A Network Structure to Explicitly Reduce Confusion Errors in Semantic Segmentation

Semantic segmentation models often struggle with confusion errors between visually similar classes, leading to misclassifications that reduce overall performance. This paper introduces a novel network architecture specifically designed to address this challenge by explicitly modeling and reducing inter-class confusion. Our approach incorporates a Confusion Reduction Module (CRM) that operates alongside the standard segmentation pipeline to identify potential confusion patterns during training. The CRM learns class-specific features that enhance discriminative capabilities particularly between frequently confused class pairs. Through extensive experimentation on benchmark datasets including Cityscapes, PASCAL VOC, and ADE20K, we demonstrate that our approach consistently reduces confusion errors by 15-20% compared to baseline architectures while maintaining computational efficiency. The proposed method is architecture-agnostic and can be integrated with various backbone networks. Ablation studies confirm that the performance improvements stem from the model's enhanced ability to distinguish between semantically similar classes rather than general accuracy gains. Our approach not only improves mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) scores but also delivers more consistent performance across all classes, making it particularly valuable for applications requiring high reliability across the entire label space.

Edge-aware Graph Representation Learning and Reasoning for Face Parsing

Face parsing, the task of pixel-level facial component segmentation, remains challenging due to complex structural relationships between facial elements and boundary ambiguities. This paper introduces a novel Edge-aware Graph Representation Learning and Reasoning (EGRR) framework that explicitly models both the local and global contextual relationships of facial components. Our approach integrates graph representation learning with edge-aware feature enhancement to improve boundary precision and component coherence. The framework consists of three key components: (1) a facial graph construction module that represents facial elements as nodes with learnable semantic relationships; (2) an edge-aware feature refinement mechanism that leverages boundary cues to enhance discrimination between adjacent facial regions; and (3) a graph reasoning module that propagates information across the facial topology to ensure global consistency. Extensive experiments on popular benchmarks including CelebAMask-HQ, LaPa, and Helen demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, with particular improvements in boundary accuracy and fine-grained facial component segmentation. Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of each proposed component. Our approach not only advances face parsing performance but also provides interpretable representations of facial structures that could benefit related facial analysis tasks.

3D-LaneNet: End-to-End 3D Multiple Lane Detection

This paper presents 3D-LaneNet, a novel end-to-end deep learning framework for detecting multiple lanes in 3D space from a single monocular image. Unlike traditional approaches that detect lanes in the 2D image plane, our method directly predicts the 3D positions of lane markings in the world coordinate system, providing crucial information for autonomous driving applications. The proposed network architecture consists of an image encoding backbone followed by a specialized dual-pathway decoder that simultaneously processes features in both top-view and perspective view spaces. We introduce a geometry-aware lane parameterization that enables accurate lane representation in 3D space while maintaining computational efficiency. To train our model, we develop a comprehensive loss function that addresses the challenges of 3D lane detection, including depth ambiguity and structural consistency. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that 3D-LaneNet significantly outperforms state-of-the-art 2D lane detection methods when evaluated on 3D metrics, while maintaining competitive performance on traditional 2D benchmarks. Our approach shows particular robustness to challenging scenarios such as curved roads, changing elevations, and adverse weather conditions, making it suitable for real-world autonomous driving systems.

Towards Open Ad Hoc Teamwork Using Graph-based Policy Learning

Ad hoc teamwork addresses the challenge of designing agents that can collaborate effectively with previously unknown teammates. While significant progress has been made in this field, most existing approaches assume fixed team compositions and known teammate types. This paper introduces a novel graph-based policy learning framework that extends ad hoc teamwork to open settings, where agents must adapt to varying team sizes and previously unseen teammate behaviors. Our approach leverages graph neural networks to encode agent interactions and team dynamics in a permutation-invariant manner, enabling generalization across different team configurations. We formulate the open ad hoc teamwork problem and propose a scalable architecture that combines graph attention mechanisms with policy learning to reason about diverse teammate behaviors. Through extensive evaluation across multiple cooperative domains, including predator-prey and collaborative navigation tasks, we demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms baseline methods when collaborating with both familiar and previously unseen teammates. Results show that our graph-based policy can effectively transfer knowledge between different team compositions and adapt to novel teammates without requiring retraining. This work represents an important step toward truly flexible autonomous agents capable of ad hoc collaboration in open multi-agent systems.

Hierarchical Attention Networks for Medical Image Segmentation

Medical image segmentation remains a challenging task requiring precise delineation of anatomical structures and pathological regions. In this paper, we introduce Hierarchical Attention Networks (HANs), a novel deep learning architecture designed specifically for medical image segmentation tasks. Our approach leverages multi-scale feature representations combined with attention mechanisms operating at different hierarchical levels to effectively capture both local details and global contextual information. The proposed network employs a coarse-to-fine segmentation strategy where higher-level attention modules guide lower-level ones, enabling the model to focus on anatomically relevant regions while suppressing background noise. We evaluate HANs on multiple medical imaging modalities including MRI, CT, and ultrasound across diverse anatomical structures. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art segmentation approaches, achieving significant improvements in Dice similarity coefficient (up to 4.2%), Hausdorff distance, and boundary F1 score. Additionally, ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of each hierarchical attention component. The proposed architecture shows particular promise for segmenting small structures and handling cases with limited training data, addressing key challenges in clinical applications. Our code and trained models will be made publicly available to facilitate further research.

Task-Driven Super Resolution: Object Detection in Low-resolution Images

This paper introduces a novel task-driven approach to super resolution specifically designed to enhance object detection performance in low-resolution images. While traditional super resolution methods focus on perceptual quality metrics, we propose a framework that directly optimizes the super resolution process for the downstream task of object detection. Our method integrates a differentiable super resolution network with an object detection pipeline, allowing end-to-end training that prioritizes accurate object localization and classification over general image quality. Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate that our task-driven approach significantly outperforms conventional super resolution techniques when evaluated on object detection metrics, improving mean Average Precision (mAP) by up to 18% on low-resolution test images. We conduct extensive ablation studies to analyze the contribution of different components and demonstrate that our method is particularly effective for small objects and in surveillance scenarios with naturally occurring low-resolution imagery. This work highlights the importance of task-specific super resolution and provides a foundation for future research in task-oriented image enhancement techniques.

Abstract

This paper presents a novel approach to enhance monocular depth estimation in 360° images through a combination of architectural innovations and learning strategies. We introduce a Non-local Dense Prediction Transformer (NDPT) framework that effectively captures long-range dependencies across the entire spherical field of view, addressing the limitations of conventional convolutional networks in handling distortions inherent in equirectangular projections. Our NDPT architecture integrates self-attention mechanisms with dense prediction capabilities specifically tailored for spherical geometry. To optimize the learning process, we propose a joint supervised and self-supervised learning strategy that leverages both ground truth depth annotations and geometric consistency constraints from unlabeled data. This hybrid learning approach allows our model to benefit from explicit supervision while also learning from the rich geometric cues present in omnidirectional imagery. Extensive experiments on standard 360° depth estimation benchmarks demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, achieving improvements of up to 15% in absolute relative error and 12% in δ1 accuracy. Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of both our architectural design and learning strategy. Our approach enables more accurate depth perception for applications in virtual reality, autonomous navigation, and computational photography that rely on omnidirectional understanding of scenes.

Learning from LDA using Deep Neural Networks

This paper explores a novel approach to integrating Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) with deep neural networks to enhance topic modeling capabilities. We propose a framework where deep neural architectures learn from and extend the representational power of traditional LDA models. Our method leverages pre-trained LDA topic distributions as inputs to neural networks, enabling the discovery of more nuanced semantic relationships while preserving the interpretability advantages of probabilistic topic models. Experiments conducted on multiple text corpora demonstrate that our hybrid approach outperforms both standalone LDA and standard deep learning text representations across document classification, clustering, and information retrieval tasks. The results show significant improvements in topic coherence (15% increase) and classification accuracy (8-12% improvement) compared to baseline methods. Furthermore, our approach addresses common limitations of LDA, such as handling short texts and capturing hierarchical topic structures, while maintaining computational efficiency. This work contributes to bridging the gap between probabilistic topic modeling and deep learning, offering insights for developing more powerful text analysis systems.

On the Optimization Landscape of Tensor Decompositions

This paper investigates the geometric properties of optimization landscapes arising in low-rank tensor decomposition problems. While tensor decompositions have become fundamental tools across machine learning, signal processing, and data analysis, their non-convex optimization landscapes present significant theoretical and computational challenges. We analyze the critical point structure of several canonical tensor decomposition objectives, including CP decomposition and Tucker decomposition, establishing conditions under which these landscapes admit benign geometric properties despite their non-convexity. Our theoretical results characterize the relationship between tensor rank, dimensionality, and the prevalence of spurious local minima. We prove that under certain incoherence conditions, gradient-based methods can provably converge to global optima despite the NP-hardness of the general problem. Through careful analysis of saddle point structures, we demonstrate that many local minima in these landscapes correspond to permutation and scaling variants of the ground truth decomposition.
